newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Australia beef prices seen off in 96/97 - ABARE.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Australia beef prices seen off in 96/97 - ABARE.

text.p: The Australian Bureau of Agricultral and Resource Economics (ABARE) said on Tuesday it expects Australian beef saleyard prices to fall by 9.6 percent to average A$1.60 per kg in 1996/97 (July-June).
This compares with a premlinary A$1.77 per kg in 1995/96.

"Given the uncertainties associated with the beef market, it is estimated that there is a 75 percent probabilty that final average outcome for the saleyard indicator price will be between 126c/kg and 177c/kg," ABARE said in its quarterly outlook.
The forecast price depended on the rate and extent of herd liquidation underway in the United States, ABARE said.

It was also dependent on the extent of expected growth in Asian beef demand, continuing diversification of Australia's beef export markets, and the expected increase of supply of Australian grassfed and grainfed beef in 1996/97, it said.
Exports to the United States are likely to fall to 170,000 tonnes -- half of the annual export volume of the early 1990s -- due to large supplies of U.S. grassfed beef, ABARE said.

"Demand for beef in Japan is likely to be dampened, at least in the short term, by the recent contamination of beef by the E.coli bacteria, causing widespread food poisoning in the country," ABARE said.
